items.title: Anne Hathaway's Best Quotes About Motherhood, Parenting With Adam Shulman
items.summary:
Anne Hathaway tends to keep her kids out of the public eye, but that hasn’t stopped her from occasionally opening up about how they have changed her life.

The actress wed Adam Shulman in September 2012 in California, four years before welcoming their first child.

In July 2019, the Princess Diaries star announced that baby No. 2 was on the way after experiencing fertility struggles. “It’s not for a movie,” the New York native captioned her Instagram baby bump debut at the time. “All kidding aside, for everyone going through infertility and conception hell, please know it was not a straight line to either of my pregnancies. Sending you extra love.”

The Devil Wears Prada star’s second son arrived five months later. While Us Weekly revealed the little one’s name, Jack, in January 2020, she waited until October of that same year to confirm the moniker .

In June 2026, Hathaway announced that she was expecting baby No. 3. The little one’s arrival was revealed that November when the actress was spotted with an infant strapped to her chest while out and about in NYC. ( Us reached out to Hathaway’s rep for comment.)

items.title: Susan Smith's Ex David Had 'Dark Days' After She Killed Their 2 Sons
items.summary:
More than 30 years after Susan Smith was arrested for drowning her two young sons, her ex-husband, David Smith , is looking back on the moment he learned what happened to their children.

“It was a blur. I didn’t know which way was up and which way was down, left or right. It was a blur. For years afterwards, too,” David tells Us .

David adds that the time following the tragedy is also unclear. “Family get-togethers, or events or something that we did, and I just don’t remember,” he says.

David’s current wife, Tiffany Smith , tells Us that there “were a lot of dark days” for her husband.

NC Mom Found After 24 Years: What We Know About Michele Hundley Smith 

“He had a lot of dark times, and I had to be persistent and keep pushing him,” she explains.

David adds that “you don’t ever think about having to bury a child” as a parent.

“We’re supposed to outlive our children. They’re supposed to bury us,” he continues. “They were my reason for living every day. And then she just took that away in a blink of an eye, and I just had to start finding other reasons to keep moving forward.”

He says that things were “really bad for the first five years,” and it was difficult to “not take my life.”

Susan, 55, was sentenced to life in prison in 1995, one year after she rolled her car into John D. Long Lake in South Carolina with her sons, Michael and Alex, strapped inside. The boys were just 3 years old and 14 months old at the time.

She initially made national headlines when she claimed that a man carjacked her and took her sons. Susan and David appeared on TV as she made a…

items.title: Mandy Moore Celebrates 8th Wedding Anniversary With Husband Taylor Goldsmith
items.summary:
Mandy Moore and Taylor Goldsmith fell head over heels for each other, and their quiet love story slowly captured all of our hearts.

The This Is U s alum didn’t stop believing in love after she finalized her divorce from Ryan Adams . Moore and Adams called it quits in January 2015 following nearly six years of marriage. She and Goldsmith met through Instagram in May 2015 after she outed herself as a fan of his band, Dawes, by posting the cover of one of their albums. When Goldsmith noticed his famous new fan, the two began DMing and bonded over their shared love of music.

The twosome got engaged in September 2017, and it was only fitting that Moore said they were planning a low-key wedding. “I don’t think I’m going to have a big, old affair,” Moore told Us one month later. “I think it will be small, and quiet, and private.”

In November 2018, Moore and Goldsmith exchanged vows at sunset in the actress’ backyard in front of friends and family, including This Is Us costars Milo Ventimiglia , Chrissy Metz and Sterling K. Brown .

items.summary:
The Brady Bunch alum Barry Williams gave his all throughout Dancing With the Stars , which admittedly took him a while to recuperate from after leaving the ballroom competition.

“At Dancing with the Stars , I brought out 100 percent of everything; everything I had. I have never been so tested,” Williams, 72, said on a recent episode of the “Pop Culture Preservation Society” podcast . “I’m not going to lie: There was a year of recovery after those two, three months.”

Williams danced with DWTS pro Peta Murgatroyd on 2023’s season 32, finishing in seventh place.

“It was really hard on my knees, et cetera,” he said, adding that he “loved” the journey overall. “It was a great experience. It was so challenging and so much fun.”

DWTS’ Barry Williams Reflects on ‘Tough Judge’ Derek Hough’s Critiques 

While Williams went into DWTS following a professional career in musical theater, he felt like a complete novice when it came to the ballroom and Latin styles.

“There’s no way that you can actually practice for ballroom. It is completely different,” the actor acknowledged. “It is like what pop music dancing is to ballet is what ballroom is to pop, and so it helps to have a really, really great partner, and I did, [and] that is what really carried it. Whatever it was going to be, I just knew that I would leave it all on the dance floor. [I had a] great time.”

items.title: Stephen Baldwin Opens Up About ‘Life-Changing’ Heart Disease Scare
items.summary:
Stephen Baldwin gained a new perspective on life after he experienced a frightening medical emergency over the summer.

“I was at home, and I got this kind of fluttering on my chest, directly over my heart,” Baldwin, 60, told People in an interview published on Wednesday, November 18. “It was almost like if I took a feather and I tickled the back of your hand. I felt this weird kind of tickling sensation on my skin, directly under my pectoral muscle.”

The Usual Suspects actor said he experienced the sensation again multiple times throughout the night, approximately every four hours.

“I woke up the next day, and immediately it was there again,” he recalled. “Nothing intense, no pain. Just a strange fluttering.”

Baldwin said he became alarmed when the fluttering increased to every two hours.

“I’m not a doctor, but I’ve played one on TV. And common sense would say, you know, my body’s saying something and I don’t know what it is,” he continued. “So, ​​I’m getting a little nervous.”

When Did Hailey Bieber Have a Mini Stroke? Her Health Scare Explained 

Thankfully, Baldwin already had an aortic specialist after his daughter Hailey Bieber encouraged him to keep an eye on his heart health four years ago. (Baldwin’s father had an aortic aneurysm, a balloon-like bulge in the aorta, before he died from lung cancer at age 55. Aortic issues can be hereditary.)

Baldwin recalled texting his specialist, who called him right away.

“He wastes no time. He just literally says to me these life-changing words: ‘Listen to me, and do exactly as I tell you. When you hang up this phone…’…

items.title: Is it finally OK to be frank about 2000s pop culture? ‘It was profoundly, cheerfully horrible to women’

In a 2008 episode of BBC Two’s comedy panel show Never Mind the Buzzcocks, the choreographer Arlene Phillips – the only woman on the programme – was told by the host Simon Amstell: “You look like you run a good whore house.” In reply, Phillips told a story with what appeared to be faux sincerity: while working with big stars, she explained, she would sometimes be asked to find dancers with “very special abilities” who might want to party after filming. Another panellist, the TV presenter Dermot O’Leary, mimed picking up a phone and said: “When you’re dancing tonight, do you mind having sex afterwards?” Everyone laughed.

Russell Brand’s imprisonment for rape and sexual assault this week, and allegations of sexual misconduct against the comedian and children’s author David Walliams have prompted scrutiny not only of the men involved, but of those who appeared to enable them. The chatshow host Jonathan Ross has apologised for a 2004 joke, in which he described the 15-year-old British comedy awards as being “like most 15-year-olds: drunk, unpredictable and probably going home with David Walliams”. The latter has denied the allegations made against him in reporting by the Guardian and ITV…

items.title: I saw how brightly stars like Russell Brand could shine, but there is darkness in the shadows | Sophie Heawood
items.summary:
After years of celebrity interviews, I have learned not to be fooled by the allure of fame. We never really know them – we know what they want us to know

As I sat in Southwark crown court, listening to the final day of Russell Brand’s trial, there was one subject that came up repeatedly, invoked as often by his defence as the prosecution. I don’t mean sex or coercion, but fame. It ran through every victim impact statement and loomed so large in the courtroom that it felt as if it was almost on trial itself.

I’m an entertainment journalist who has been covering celebrities for more than 20 years – as long as Brand has been one – and I have written about him at various stages of his career. But I went to Southwark crown court as a member of the public who wanted to see justice done. For the women he had hurt, for the ones who couldn’t get as far as the courtroom, and for all of us who came of age at a time when rape culture was so fast and furious that young women mistook it for a joke that we were in on. In the age of lads’ mags, sex felt cheapened, yet somehow we were the ones who ended up paying for this. So it was doubly strange to sit in court and feel somehow complicit in it - in how this media culture had encouraged Russell Brand.

Continue reading...
items.t: I saw how brightly stars like Russell Brand could shine, but there is darkness in the shadows | Sophie Heawood

items.title: Two courtrooms, one celebrity: how did the Russell Brand case compare with the rape trial next door?
items.summary:
One was a high-profile defendant watched by more than 100 journalists. Another was an unknown man who preyed on a girl almost half his age. Their stories played out minutes apart, one entirely out of the spotlight

What is going on inside Russell Brand’s head as he arrives at court for the start of his rape trial? He sees the dozens of cameras and journalists lined outside Southwark crown court, many of whom have been waiting since before 7am, and he tells himself that the media are all against him. “It seems to me that they believe that I am guilty, and that this should be the rubber-stamping of the process of my destruction.”

He walks with his wife, Laura, and his bodyguard past the photographers, “clickering, clackering, snickering paparazzi, like locusts, peculiar concoctions, not fully humans”, and up into the court, where he is suddenly overwhelmed by “the presence of something very beautiful, grace”. “In a situation like I’m in, it’s impossible not to turn to God. Truth and justice are the only things that can save me,” he thinks.

Continue reading...
items.t: Two courtrooms, one celebrity: how did the Russell Brand case compare with the rape trial next door?
